title: How Well Do You Know David and Goliath?
subtitle: The shepherd, the giant, and one famous stone.
about: One shepherd boy, one giant, one sling, and a whole army too afraid to move. It is one of scripture's most famous stories, and also one of its clearest pictures of what faith looks like in front of something impossibly large.

verses.text: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin: but I come to thee in the name of Jehovah of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

questions.text: Which army did Goliath fight for?

options.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:4 says the champion came out of the camp of the Philistines, and his name was Goliath.
Egypt was Israel's old enemy from the Exodus, but Goliath was a Philistine.
The Amalekites fought Israel too, but Goliath belonged to the Philistine army.
Assyria rose to power later. In David's day the threat was the Philistines.
1 Samuel 17:4 names him Goliath, of Gath, one of the chief Philistine cities.
Gaza was a Philistine city, but Goliath came from Gath.
Jericho was an Israelite city famous for its fallen walls, not Goliath's home.
Bethlehem was David's hometown, not the giant's.

questions.text: What work was David doing for his father before he faced Goliath?

options.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:15 says David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
David was a shepherd, not a fisherman.
David was tending his father's flock, not building.
His older brothers were in the army, but David was still keeping sheep at home.

questions.text: Why did David come to the battle line in the first place?

options.text: He was sent to bring food to his brothers
options.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:17-18 says Jesse sent David with grain and bread for his brothers and cheese for their commander.

options.text: He was drafted into the army
options.explanation: David was not drafted. His father sent him to check on his brothers and bring them food.
He came as an errand boy with supplies, then heard Goliath's taunts once he arrived.

options.text: The king summoned him to fight
options.explanation: Saul did not summon him to fight. David volunteered after he saw the standoff.

questions.text: Who was the king of Israel during this battle?

options.explanation: Saul was Israel's first king and led the army that stood frozen before Goliath in 1 Samuel 17.
David would become king later. At this point he was still a young shepherd.
Solomon was David's son and reigned generations of stories later.
Samuel was the prophet who anointed Saul and David, but he was not the king.

questions.text: What did King Saul offer David to wear into the fight?

options.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:38 says Saul put his own armor on David, with a helmet of brass and a coat of mail.
Saul offered armor for battle, not a robe.
There was no lion's skin. Saul gave David his own armor, which David then took off.
Saul did not give him a crown. He offered his armor, which David found too clumsy.

questions.text: How many smooth stones did David choose from the brook?

options.explanation: He took more than one, even though he only needed a single throw.
Close, but the text gives a different number.
1 Samuel 17:40 says David chose five smooth stones out of the brook and put them in his shepherd's bag.
Seven shows up often in Scripture, but here David gathered five stones.

questions.text: What weapon did David use to bring Goliath down?

options.explanation: David was not an archer in this story. He used a sling.
Goliath carried a huge spear, but David did not fight with one.
1 Samuel 17:49-50 says David struck the Philistine with a sling and a stone, and there was no sword in his hand.
David had no sword when he knocked Goliath down. He used a sling first.

questions.text: Where did the stone strike Goliath?

options.explanation: The stone did not hit his chest, which his armor protected.
1 Samuel 17:49 says the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth.
The blow that felled him struck his forehead, not his knee.
The stone hit his forehead, the one place his heavy armor left open.

questions.text: After Goliath fell, what did David use to cut off the giant's head?

options.explanation: David had no sword of his own. He grabbed the giant's.
1 Samuel 17:51 says David took Goliath's sword and cut off his head with it.
He did not borrow a spear. He used the sword that belonged to Goliath.
A staff could not do this. David used the giant's own sword.

questions.text: In David's own words, in whose name did he say he came against Goliath?

options.text: In the name of the LORD of hosts
options.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:45 says David came in the name of Jehovah of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel.

options.text: In the name of King Saul
options.explanation: David trusted God, not Saul, and said so plainly before the fight.

options.text: In the name of his father Jesse
options.explanation: David did not invoke his father. He came in the name of the LORD of hosts.
David made clear the victory was not about himself but about God.

questions.text: When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, what did they do?

options.explanation: They did not surrender. They turned and ran.
1 Samuel 17:51 says when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.
No second giant came forward. The army ran away.
There was no peace treaty. The Philistines fled and Israel pursued them.

scoring.perfectMessage: A perfect score. Not one stone missed.
